commands.summary: 5/5 runtime cost tests passed: zero duplicate forward on miss+build, zero forward on certified reuse, immutable NormalizationConstants caching, 3 identity modes configuration, exhaustive mutation detection (weights, BN buffers, training mode, grad, hooks, mean/std), and baseline benchmarking
5/5 runtime tests passed cleanly without regression
All 324/324 unit tests passed across entire repository test suite
214/214 protected files verified clean and intact

requirement_evidence.evidence: Actual reference forward calls are tracked explicitly via ReferenceOwner.forward_calls_count and RuntimeCounters.reference_forward_calls. On miss+build, exactly one trusted inference occurs and certificate build reuses the issued anchor receipt. On certified reuse hit, delta forward calls is strictly zero. Verified by test_c01_forward_calls_count_and_zero_duplicate_work.

NormalizationConstants are verified and cached in ReferenceOwner._cached_norm_constants. Accessors return fresh read-only copies with writeable=False flag; attempting to mutate throws ValueError. Mutating internal arrays invalidates preprocessing ID and raises IdentityError. Verified by test_c02_immutable_constants_caching.

Implemented IdentityCheckMode enum with STRONG_PER_QUERY, OWNED_GENERATION, and CORE_INFERENCE. ReferenceOwner supports runtime switching via set_identity_mode(). Model ownership and encapsulation assumptions documented in identity_modes_review.md. Verified by test_c03_identity_modes_configuration.

Exhaustive mutation test suite verifies immediate detection and fail-closed IdentityError for: (1) model weights mutation, (2) BatchNorm running_mean/var mutation, (3) model.train() mode switch, (4) requires_grad=True mutation, (5) forward hooks injection, and (6) preprocessing mean/std array mutation. Trade-off documented: OWNED_GENERATION mode detects mutations at init and generation boundary invalidation. Verified by test_c04_exhaustive_mutation_detection.

Micro-benchmarking measured isolated component latencies on idle host (100 iterations, 10 warmup): pure PyTorch forward (0.182 ms), full assert_identity SHA-256 digest (1.394 ms), fast shallow check (0.094 ms), and NumPy normalization (0.014 ms). Verified by test_c05_and_c06_runtime_cost_benchmark_and_artifacts.

All three standard baselines reported side-by-side in runtime_cost_validation.json and identity_modes_review.md: M00 Core inference (0.303 ms, 1.00x), M01 Strong wrapper (1.814 ms, 5.98x slower), and M16 Owned reference (0.439 ms, 4.13x faster than M01, 1.45x of M00). No cherry-picked or inflated identity overhead.
Zero modification to interval bounds, coordinate enclosures, NumericalCapability gates, or rounding rules. All mathematical and numerical semantics remain strictly identical to frozen specifications.

scientific_dispositions.H18_finite_horizon: CONFIRMED: Atomic state commit and fail-closed error handling eliminate non-deterministic drift.
scientific_dispositions.H20_identity_overhead: CONFIRMED: Full per-query SHA-256 state digest incurs 1.394 ms overhead (76.8% of total inference time), causing 5.98x slowdown over bare PyTorch M00.
scientific_dispositions.H21_owned_reference: CONFIRMED: Owned-reference architecture (M16) achieves 4.13x speedup over M01 by performing fast shallow checks during active generation and reserving full SHA-256 audits for generation boundaries and initialization.
scientific_dispositions.H22_duplicate_elimination: CONFIRMED: Exactly one trusted forward on miss+build, and zero forwards on certified reuse.

limitations: In OWNED_GENERATION mode, arbitrary in-process memory mutation of weights by malicious threads within a generation is not detected until invalidate() is called; applications requiring protection against hostile intra-process code execution must use STRONG_PER_QUERY mode.
Benchmark measurements reflect CPU execution (Intel/AMD x86_64 CPU float32); GPU-accelerated backends will exhibit different relative overhead ratios.
